title: Microplastics Analysis in Marine Organisms and Sediment Using FTIR
author: Tanoiri, Barrientos, et al.

steps.title: Wear non‑plastic protective clothing
steps.instruction: Wear 100 % cotton clothing or white lab coats with minimal skin exposure, use gloves and goggles, and clean all clothing of foreign particles with adhesive tape before any microplastic extraction.

steps.title: Prepare equipment and record masses
steps.instruction: Wash all laboratory equipment with distilled water immediately before use, work under sterile, dust‑proof conditions, then record the masses of the pipe (A), aluminum cap (B) and lower plug (C). Fill the hole in the lower plug with distilled water, transfer the water to a graduated cylinder and record the hole volume (D).

steps.title: Prepare carbonate elimination reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare two carbonate‑elimination reagents (α and β). Reagent α contains: Formic acid 20 v/v % (CAS 64‑18‑6), Iron(II) sulfate heptahydrate 10 mg mL⁻¹ (CAS 7782‑63‑0), Decamethyl‑cyclopentasiloxane (D5) 20 µL mL⁻¹ (CAS 541‑02‑6), Sodium dodecyl sulfate 1 w/v % (CAS 151‑21‑3), and 3‑Methyl‑1‑butanol (3M1B) 40 µL mL⁻¹ (CAS 7782‑63‑0). Add a defoaming mixture of D5 (or propylene glycol) together with 3M1B to reduce foam; ethanol may be used as a short‑lived alternative.

steps.title: Add carbonate reagent and monitor reaction
steps.instruction: Place the sample in the lower stopper, record its mass, insert the lower plug into the pipe, then add 3 mL of reagent α per gram of sample and cap the upper end. Wait until bubbling stops, then add an additional 0.1 mL of reagent α to ensure acidic conditions before proceeding.

steps.title: Fenton decomposition with ice cooling
steps.instruction: Prepare 1–2 L of ice water in a beaker. Add 30 mL of 35 % hydrogen peroxide (CAS 7722‑84‑1) per gram of sample to the fractionator, then immerse the fractionator in the ice water for 24 h (ice may melt but is not replaced). Agitate with a mixer, then let the fractionator stand 24 h at room temperature in water, followed by 72 h at 50 °C (immersed in water to prevent overheating). Finally, bring the fractionator back to room temperature.

steps.title: Alkaline KOH digestion
steps.instruction: Prepare a 50 w/v % potassium hydroxide solution (CAS 1310‑58‑3) containing 0.2 mg mL⁻¹ EDTA‑2Na (CAS 139‑33‑3), noting the heat released on dissolution. Using a filter syringe, add 5 mL of this KOH‑EDTA solution per gram of sample while observing the reaction. Incubate the fractionator at 50 °C for 1 day, then return to room temperature and vortex‑mix the sample.

steps.title: Perform density separation with NaI
steps.instruction: Prepare sodium iodide (NaI, CAS 7681‑82‑5) solutions of specific gravities 1.8 and 1.6 by dissolving NaI in 500 mL distilled water (1 L beaker) and adjusting with additional NaI until the desired SG is reached (measure SG with a 10 mL sample). Filter each solution through filter paper finer than the smallest target MP. Measure the weight of the fractionator with sample (E) and the solution height (h). Calculate the current SG using the provided formula, then add 1.8 NaI volume = 5 (1.6 – d) V to reach a final SG of 1.6. Add 1.6 NaI to bring the total volume to 150 mL, stand the fractionator upright for ≥3 h. Fill a 1 L beaker to 600 mL with 1.6 NaI solution, loosen the lower stopper just enough to prevent leakage, close the upper valve, immerse the lower part of the fractionator in the 1.6 NaI bath and gently open the lower stopper. Open the upper valve slightly, pour half of the NaI from the fractionator into the external bath, then close the valve. Close the lower part with a clean plug and reopen the upper valve. Repeat the addition of 150 mL 1.6 NaI twice (first and second cycles); on the third cycle proceed directly to filtration without further NaI addition.

steps.title: Add SDS and incubate filter
steps.instruction: Using a filter syringe, add 1 mL of 1 % SDS solution to the filter holder, cover with aluminum foil, and incubate for 2 h at 50 °C. Afterwards, attach the filter holder to a vacuum filtration bottle and perform vacuum filtration.

steps.title: Wash filter with distilled water
steps.instruction: Rinse the filter with distilled water after SDS treatment and proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Treat filter with NaUT solution
steps.instruction: Pre‑cool the sealed container that will hold the filter holder to –20 °C. Prepare a NaUT solution containing 8 % NaOH, 8 % urea and 6.5 % w/v thiourea. Using a filter syringe, add 1 mL of this NaUT solution to the funnel, cover, and place the filter holder in the pre‑cooled airtight container to freeze at –20 °C. Once solidified, remove the holder, vortex‑mix, then allow it to melt back to liquid and filter under reduced pressure. Wash the filter with distilled water and store the PTFE filter.

steps.title: Handle PTFE filter to prevent curling
steps.instruction: When drying PTFE filters, restrain the edges to avoid curling and seal the filter to prevent contamination or sample loss.
